summary: beaver-ui-drawer ships a hidden host-fingerprinting beacon disguised as a UI toolkit
details: package.json describes beaver-ui-drawer as a 'visual components' UI toolkit and index.js exports a no-op BeaverUiDrawer class, but index.js also appends a swallowed 'try { require("./setup"); } catch (_) {}' that auto-loads a 76KB telemetry runtime on require. setup.js schedules a process.nextTick bootstrap that reads os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), pid and node version, hashes them into an installId, and passes the fingerprint to lib/telemetry.js which opens an HTTPS transport whose destination is built at runtime via a ServiceDiscovery class using DNS-based endpoint discovery. Both setup.js and lib/telemetry.js access the os module through split-string keys (os["host"+"name"](), os["user"+"Info"]().username, os["plat"+"form"](), const _p = (k) => os[k]()) so the strings 'hostname' and 'userInfo' never appear literally, and the 76KB transport contains zero plain URL or hostname literals. The advertised UI-toolkit purpose has no relationship to the shipped code, which is only a fingerprint collector plus a runtime-resolved exfiltration transport.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
